title: Ang 151: Gauri begins
hookLine: the Granth's largest raga opens with Guru Nanak
tomorrow: how do you lose a whole day without noticing?
last: FAMILY · THE LONG RUN · CLOSING HYMNS.

lines: A BOX OF BOOKS. A SLEEPING KID.
cards: A moving box full of books. A sleeping kid carried up the stairs. A grandparent's hand, when they lean on you for the first time.
Heavy things come in different shapes. So what's heavier than anything you've ever lifted? Gauri opens on ang 151, and Guru Nanak's first line in it weighs two things against each other.

teach.b: Gauri runs from ang 151 all the way to 346, the largest raga in the Granth, and Guru Nanak opens it with a scale.
In paraphrase: the fear of God is very heavy, a great weight; the mind's own cleverness is light, and it speaks light words. Bhau, the word here, is fear, but not the kind that makes you run.
It's closer to awe: the weight of standing before something real, the kind that makes you careful. And the clever mind?
It's quick and it's light, and it talks. That's the contrast. Light talk floats.
Awe sits down in you and stays.
Notice how this week fits the scale. A protector everywhere, so fear of anything else runs out. An I that's given away.
A jewel kept hidden. A month for clean hands.
Another's due, off the plate. A mosque made of mercy. None of it is clever.
All of it is heavy, in the good way, the way a hand on your shoulder is heavy.

how: Sikhs reading the Granth in order reach Gauri after Majh ki Var; Gauri hymns are sung in kirtan, and the long Sukhmani, read daily by some Sikhs, sits inside this raga.

games.q: you're deciding whether to quit a club. your brain has made three clever pro-and-con lists. what would the first line of Gauri ask?
o: go with the longest list; the heavier side has more reasons.
set the clever talk aside and ask what carries real weight.
don't decide; fear of choosing wrong should stop you.
games.why: on ang 151, cleverness is light and talks light words; awe is the heavy thing. the scale tips toward what's weighty, not what's clever.

practice: If you can, open ang 151 and read the first line aloud, slowly. Then say two words out loud, one at a time: first light, then heavy. Notice which one your body settles into, and stay there for the rest of the sit.
